chunks: Muhammad ibn Ya'qub, from Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Ali ibn Abi Hamzah, from Abu Basir, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

When you stand at Arafat, draw near to the hills, and the hills are the mountains, for the Prophet (peace be upon him) said: 'Those who stand at the Arak trees have no Hajj,' meaning those who stand at the Arak trees.

key_terms.الْأَرَكَ: Arak trees, a type of tree common in the Arafat plain
key_terms.عَرَفَاتٍ: Arafat, the plain where the central rite of Hajj (Wuquf) takes place
key_terms.لَا حَجَّ لَهُمْ: They have no Hajj (implying deficiency or invalidity depending on context)

ai.seo_question: What is the recommended location for standing at Arafat according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Istibsar clarifies the geographical specifics of the Arafat standing (wuquf), distinguishing between the general plain and the elevated hills (hubb) to ensure the ritual's validity. It highlights the scholarly nuance that while standing at the Arak trees is often associated with the Prophet’s final sermon, proximity to the hills is preferred to align with the Sunnah, reflecting the Shia emphasis on precise ritual geography. This guidance underscores the importance of following the Prophet’s specific instructions regarding the physical location of the pillar of Hajj.
